items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (buildWindowSpecSQL, validateWindowName) and the formatting matches the codebase. But the WINDOW chunk in all five dialects uses a single-letter param in logic: `windows.map((w) => sql`${sql.identifier(w.name)} as (...)`)`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Shared spec builder and validator in window.ts, reused by each dialect, as the conventions ask. But each dialect's .window() is not thin: it adds an unrequested callback form with a SelectionProxyHandler block, copied five times.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are validated at the boundary: preceding/following reject negative, non-integer and NaN; ntile/nthValue errors include the function name and the value; frame order is checked; window names are checked in both .window() and .over(). Tests cover all of these.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: Purely additive: optional `windows?: WindowDefinition[]` added to all five *SelectConfig types, the same .window() on pg/mysql/sqlite/gel/singlestore, and windowsSql is undefined when unused, so existing SQL is unchanged. Existing tests (P2P) all pass.
